props.title: Bedknobs and Broomsticks
props.initialSlug: Apprentice witch, kids fight Nazis with magic & music

sections.content: Bedknobs and Broomsticks represents Disney's ambitious attempt to recreate the magic-meets-reality formula that made Mary Poppins (1964) such a sensation. Set during WWII, this underappreciated gem combines live-action with animation, featuring Angela Lansbury as apprentice witch Miss Price who protects British children from the Nazi invasion using enchanted objects. The film showcases groundbreaking special effects for its time, particularly in the legendary Portobello Road sequence and the animated underwater kingdom of Naboombu. Director Robert Stevenson, who also helmed Mary Poppins, brings his signature blend of whimsy and technical innovation.

sections.content: The film's creation story reflects a fascinating period in Disney's history. Originally planned as a larger production, many songs by Sherman Brothers were cut, though classics like "Substitutiary Locomotion" and "Portobello Road" remained. The 2021 restoration brought back several deleted scenes and musical numbers, including "A Step in the Right Direction," showcasing Angela Lansbury's full performance as originally intended. This positions the film alongside other ambitious Disney productions of the era like Chitty Chitty Bang Bang (1968) and The Happiest Millionaire (1967).

The film's wartime setting distinguishes it from other Disney fantasies, addressing serious themes through a magical lens. Miss Price's determination to use witchcraft to defend Britain parallels real-world WWII home front efforts. This combination of fantasy and historical context influenced later films like Pan's Labyrinth (2006) and The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe (2005), which also use magical elements to process war's impact on children. sections.content: The animated sequence in Naboombu showcases Disney's technical prowess, combining traditional animation with live actors years before Who Framed Roger Rabbit (1988) perfected the technique. The underwater soccer match remains a technical achievement, influencing later hybrid films like Space Jam (1996) and Enchanted (2007). David Tomlinson's interaction with animated characters set new standards for actor performance with invisible co-stars.
